subject.title: fix: prevent operational notices from leaking to source chats

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `messages.operationalReplies` and fail-closed operator-session redirect as a public core delivery contract?
rationale: Correctness repairs cannot decide whether a new public config, plugin dispatch signal, persistent policy, and intentional source-suppression failure mode should become supported product behavior.

options.title: Adopt after repairs
options.body: Approve the four-mode policy and fail-closed redirect, but require complete reservation rollback and bounded canonical SQLite storage before merge.

options.title: Narrow the policy
options.body: Keep only an approved `silent` mode and remove redirect plus durable `once` semantics to reduce compatibility and persistence surface.

options.title: Decline the contract
options.body: Keep existing always-deliver behavior and close the PR if maintainers do not want a global operational-notice policy.

recommendation.title: Adopt after repairs
recommendation.body: Approve the four-mode policy and fail-closed redirect, but require complete reservation rollback and bounded canonical SQLite storage before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history spans the public plugin hook and central reply runtime, making this the best available owner for the product/API decision.
